parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized Rust 2021, no external crates, black-box behavior inference, exact CLI parsing, root test6.rs, Cargo project structure, set union semantics, and byte-identical output.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned implementation, build, verification, and final delivery. A single child was spawned after the initial implementation as an independent reviewer of /output, not as the primary implementer.
parallel.implementation: The parent created Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/cli.rs, src/sorted_set.rs, and test6.rs; the child later patched src/cli.rs to handle platform atoi overflow wrapping and verified the corrected parser.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration happened through the shared /output workspace: the child's parser patch directly modified the parent-created source, and the parent delivered the final project and executable after interrupting the child.
parallel.verification: The parent ran rustc, cargo build, cargo test, and byte comparisons for normal and malformed inputs; the child additionally built direct parser checkers and confirmed the overflow parser behavior matched after its patch.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final artifact was correct and officially passed, but the reviewer child did not return a completed review handoff because the parent interrupted it while it was still active.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same requirements: pure Rust 2021, std-only implementation, exact argv[1] parsing, root test6.rs, module-backed Cargo project, and exact output formatting.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single serial agent owned probing, implementation, project assembly, local verification, and final delivery without delegation or subagent handoffs.
serial.implementation: The serial run created Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/atoi.rs, src/sorted_set.rs, and test6.rs, with an atoi-like parser and a BTreeSet-backed SortedSet implementation.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All code was integrated in one local patch, compiled to /output/test6, built as a Cargo release binary, and reported as the final deliverable.
serial.verification: The serial agent probed reference outputs, checked malformed and overflow-like arguments, ran rustc, cargo build --release, cargo test, and byte comparisons against the compiled C++ binary.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished required behavior is visible at closure; the current official evaluator marks the serial artifact as passing all cases.

comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had one continuous context and no cross-agent interface contract or result transfer to manage.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a parent-child review boundary and shared-workspace transfer; serial had no inter-agent context or interface boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent implemented the Cargo project and an initial parser, while the child later corrected overflow behavior in src/cli.rs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented the project once with src/atoi.rs already covering the common overflow shape it had probed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's final parser correctness depended on a child-side fix after the parent initial implementation; serial's parser was local to the single implementation path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent waited on the reviewer several times, sent a message, then interrupted the still-running child and finalized without a child return.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; its local build, tests, and comparisons completed before final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an adverse review-result lifecycle event, while serial had a closed local result lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child patched a parent-created source file in the shared /output workspace; the patch was present in the final artifact, but there was no explicit parent reconciliation step.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all project files in one patch and then compiled and tested that same workspace.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel relied on shared-workspace side effects for the child correction, whereas serial's integration was single-owner.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent ran rustc, cargo build, cargo test, and byte comparisons; the child separately validated overflow cases and the final official evaluator passed all 40 cases.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran rustc, cargo build, cargo test, and byte comparisons; the final official evaluator also passed all 40 cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both verified sufficiently for the evaluator; parallel verification was split across parent and child while serial verification remained local.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel took 250 agent seconds, waited repeatedly on the child, interrupted it, and closed after 40/40 official success.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial took 117 agent seconds, did no delegation, and closed after 40/40 official success.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent extra budget on a review child and an interrupted handoff, but this did not prevent task completion.

outcome_analysis.explanation: This is not a discordant official outcome. The current completed status.json evaluations report that both parallel and serial passed all 40 testcases. The task-solving difference is that serial solved and verified the migration in one local workflow, while parallel used a reviewer child whose patch corrected the parent parser but whose final review result was interrupted before return.
parallel_contributors: Parent probed normal and malformed CLI behavior, implemented the project, built it, and compared outputs before spawning a reviewer.
Reviewer child found and patched the overflow parsing mismatch, then verified the corrected parser behavior before being interrupted.
serial_contributors: Single agent probed normal, malformed, and overflow-like arguments before implementation.
Single agent compiled, tested, byte-compared, and finalized without any delegated result lifecycle.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel initially had an overflow parser bug in src/cli.rs, while serial implemented the overflow-compatible parser during its single implementation pass; the parallel child fixed this before official evaluation.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; the retained pattern is a process adverse event only
